catalog.name: Gel 160
catalog.note: Maker's page: 40 g carbohydrate, about 160 kcal, a 65 g sachet, glucose to fructose 1:0.8. No caffeine in the ingredient list. Sodium is only on the nutrition panel, an image on the page; retailer listings disagree (30 mg, 100 mg), so it stays unrecorded until it is read off the pack.

catalog.name: Fast Carb Mango
catalog.note: Maker's page: 40 g carbohydrate per 500 ml in a 2:1 glucose to fructose ratio, 200 mg sodium. Nutrition table: per 100 g 378 kcal, 92.3 g carbohydrate (37.2 g sugars), 1.18 g salt; per serving (43 g, two MNSTRY spoons in 500 ml) 162.5 kcal, 39.7 g carbohydrate, 0.5 g salt. Ingredients: maltodextrin, fructose, mango fruit powder, citrates, salt; no caffeine. kcal and sodium_mg are per 43 g serving.

catalog.name: Slow Carb Heat
catalog.note: Maker's page: lemon and mango, 40 g carbohydrate per 500 ml, glucose to fructose 1:1, 260 mg sodium. The carbohydrate is isomaltulose (Palatinose, 81.4%): a slow rise in blood sugar, made for low-intensity endurance. Nutrition table: per 100 g 369 kcal, 87.6 g carbohydrate (81.5 g sugars), 1.45 g salt; per serving (46 g, two MNSTRY spoons in 500 ml an hour) 170 kcal, 40.3 g carbohydrate, 0.67 g salt. Dosage, the maker's limit: at most 46 g of powder an hour and 92 g per session (slow absorption); from the third hour, switch to FAST CARB or POWER CARB. No caffeine. kcal and sodium_mg are per 46 g serving. Limits, from the same page: max_g_per_h 46 and max_g_per_session 92 ("die maximale Dosis von 46 Gramm pro Stunde und 92 Gramm pro Einheit"); easy_only because the maker makes it for low-intensity endurance ("Ausdauereinheiten mit geringer Intensität").

catalog.name: Solid 160
catalog.note: Maker's page: 40 g carbohydrate a bar, scored to break into two 20 g halves. For long low-to-moderate sessions over 2 h, loading and recovery. Bar weight conflicts on the page (40 g sachet against a 1,920 g box of 12) and energy, sodium and caffeine are only on the nutrition image, so all four stay unrecorded until read off the pack.

gut.how: setup: what they take on a 2–3 h ride

questions.text: Which fuelling products do you use — gels, drink mixes, bars? Pick them from the catalog, or name one and the coach looks it up on the maker's page.
How do you mix a bottle of each drink mix: grams of powder, and the bottle's size in ml?
What do you take today on a 2–3 hour ride, in grams of carbohydrate an hour — none, about 30, about 60 or about 90? Has anything upset your stomach?
Caffeine: never, in races only, or in training too?

ramp.how: setup: what they take on a 2–3 h ride

fuel_band.definition: Carbohydrate during a session, by its length, how hard it is and the sport. Under an hour: none. 60–90 min: none if easy, about 30 g/h if hard. 90 min to 2.5 h: 30–60 g/h easy, about 60 hard. Over 2.5 h: 60–90 g/h of glucose and fructose. Runs take the lower half of each band; swims none. Sources: ACSM 2016; Jeukendrup 2014.

fuel_target.definition: The rate planned: the top of a hard session's band, the middle of an easy one's, never above what your gut is trained to (60 g/h until you say otherwise), plus 10 g/h on a gut-training session.

fuel_gut.definition: The most carbohydrate an hour you have taken in training without trouble. Raised 10 g/h at a time, only after a logged session at the current rate.

fuel_taken.definition: What you logged taking, in grams, from each product's label and your bottle recipe as it was that day. Self-reported: Garmin does not record it.
